warmup.text: Isaac's family has been hiding in the swamp. In Chapter 8 they have to decide whether to stay or go, and what to take with them. Before you read, think about what people carry when they leave home. What someone holds on to can show how they see the world. That is your reading lens this week.

words.text: Two roots this week. One means life. One means breath. Long ago, people thought those were almost the same thing. Look for them in words you already know. Then three endings that turn a word into a describing word. In the footprint game, say each word out loud before you pick an ending.

reading.text: Read Chapter 8 of How I Became a Ghost in your book. Keep your reading lens in mind. Watch how Isaac's family meets new people on the road, and listen for what Mister Jonah tells Isaac about the blankets. When you finish, do the Virtue Watch at the end of this tab.

assignment.text: Three questions about Chapter 8, then the first step of a new piece of writing. When a question asks why, give the reason and the words from the book that show it. In the Writer's Workshop you are only planning today. A few notes are enough.

glossary.meaning: how an author shows what a character is like
the way a person sees what is happening, based on what they have lived through

miss.brutal: Find brute inside. The silent e drops, then -al: brutal.
miss.destructive: Find destruct, from destroy. It takes -ive: destructive.
miss.expressive: Find express inside. It takes -ive: expressive.
miss.heroic: Find hero inside. It takes -ic: heroic.
miss.historic: Find history inside. The y drops, then -ic: historic.
miss.personal: Find person inside. It takes -al: personal.
miss.protective: Find protect inside. It takes -ive: protective.
miss.seasonal: Find season inside. It takes -al: seasonal.
miss.tragic: Find tragedy inside. Its end changes, then -ic: tragic.

game.title: Footprints Forward
game.sub: This week's word game · 6 footprints today
game.look: Isaac's family walks for days on a snowy road. In this game, each footprint in the snow holds a word. Pick the ending, -ive, -al or -ic, that turns it into a describing word, and the footprint lights up. Your walk keeps going all week.

do: Read the word on the footprint.
Say it with each ending.
Tap the ending that makes a real describing word.
Tap Next footprint.
how.why: These are the same three endings from Spelling, with new words. If you can build a word you have never practiced, you know the endings.

cards.title: The real walk
cards.intro: Isaac's story is made up, but the walk he is on really happened.

items.meaning: U.S. commissioners and Choctaw leaders signed the Treaty of Dancing Rabbit Creek. It gave up the Choctaw homeland in Mississippi.
Thousands of Choctaw people were moved west to what is now Oklahoma, in groups, many of them in winter.
The winter of 1831 was very hard. People on the real walk suffered from cold, hunger and sickness, and many died.

cards.note: The smallpox blankets are part of Tim Tingle's story. When you read, keep the book's events and the real history side by side.

virtue.name: perseverance
virtue.title: Perseverance or not?
virtue.intro: You just read Chapter 8. Read each moment. Tap Perseverance or Not perseverance.

items.t: Isaac's family leaves the swamp, walks all day and sleeps in the woods.
items.why: They keep going with nowhere certain to go. That is perseverance.

items.t: Isaac's mother says, “I hate to leave our friends.”
items.why: Saying how you feel is honest, but it is not perseverance yet. Perseverance is what she does next: she walks on.

items.t: Isaac carries Jumper for three days so he won't chase the walking people.
items.why: Carrying his dog day after day is hard, steady work. That is perseverance.

items.t: For three days the family follows the walkers, hiding in the tree shadows, before they step out and ask to join.
items.why: They keep watching and waiting until it is safe. Patience that keeps going is perseverance.
